biography.education: B.S. Mechanical Engineering, UT Austin 1991; Graduate Certificate Subsea Engineering, U of Houston 2016
biography.career: 25 years as oilfield mechanical engineer and project manager. Texas State Representative HD-135 (2019-2021, NW Houston/Cypress) — defeated 12-term Republican incumbent. Named Freshman of the Year by Texas Legislative Study Group. Served on Energy Resources Committee.

policyPositions.position: Winterization requirements for critical gas delivery systems with clear deadlines and third-party audits
End routine flaring/venting; permit only genuine emergencies with continuous monitoring
policyPositions.notes: Authored HB 1452 (2021) to eliminate routine flaring by 2025 — did not pass

policyPositions.position: Modern optical gas imaging, continuous monitors in hotspots
Raise surety bonds, plug orphan wells at scale tied to local hiring
Deny new permits to companies with unresolved violations
Ban industry donations to commissioners; publish calendars, recusals; livestream enforcement hearings
Explicitly 'All of the Above' — supports continued oil/gas production with stricter accountability. Not an energy-transition candidate. Positively cited Biden IRA and Bipartisan Infrastructure Law.
Voted NO on SB 8 (Heartbeat Act); Texas Choice Tracker: Pro-Choice confirmed

keyVotes.action: Filed floor amendments to add specific deadlines — rejected by Republican majority

interestGroupRatings.score: 100% (2019); 5% (2021 — low due to minority-party constraints, not changed values; Sierra Club narrative praised his anti-flaring bill)
interestGroupRatings.notes: 2019 score and authored legislation are stronger signals than 2021 numerical score

scorerNotes.energyPortfolioAxisNote: His 'All of the Above' position means he scores toward Pole B (All-of-the-Above/Fossil) on energy_portfolio, not Pole A (Renewables Priority) — despite Democratic affiliation and environmental regulation stance. He is a reform-the-industry candidate, not a replace-fossil-fuels candidate.
scorerNotes.sierraClub2021Note: Sierra Club 2021 score of 5% should NOT be read at face value. Their own narrative praises his environmental work that session. The 100% in 2019 and his authored anti-flaring legislation are stronger signals.

evidenceSummary.notes: Has actual Texas House voting record + authored energy legislation. Engineering background gives credibility on energy technical issues. All-of-the-Above framing is a genuine moderate position, not just messaging.
